prompt:
A very wide, short 8:1 strip, because it will be laid along thin floating ledges that the player stands on: one slab of floating eroded earth seen exactly side-on from a level camera, filling the whole width of the canvas from the left edge to the right edge, as a dark storybook illustration. Text-free, edge-to-edge artwork with no frame or watermark.

The slab's top is one long, flat, level surface running straight across the full width with a thin band of green above it, so the rim light is never cut: a crust of packed dusty bronze-brown soil (#4a3524 to #2a1f17) with fine grit, small crumbling clumps along its top edge and a scattering of tiny warm gold glints, lit along its upper edge by a thin warm gold rim light (#a8784a to #c89060); just below the top edge a short, slightly overhanging front lip catches the light as a warm bronze band. Below the crust the earth thickens into a solid body about a third of the canvas height, the same thickness from end to end, so the strip can be stretched or repeated; crust, body and rim light continue to both edges at the same height.

The underside does not end cleanly: the earth streams downward and slightly to the left in long, swept, wax-like drips and flowing sheets, like melting wax or worn cloth, and the lowest edges break apart into a fine spray of hard-edged dark specks and grains, with a few warm amber ones among them, each speck large enough to read clearly, drifting off to the left. The streams vary in length along the strip but none reach the bottom edge. At the far left and far right edges the underside is only the solid body; every stream starts and ends inside the strip, so copies sit side by side without a seam; and every speck has a crisp edge, none fading or blurred.

The background is one flat digital pure green (#00FF00) that fills every area the earth does not cover, edge to edge and between every stream and speck, like a green-screen backdrop: one unchanging green with no light falling on it, no paper grain, no hatching and no texture; the grain and hatching apply to the earth only. The earth uses only warm browns, umbers and near-black, and its lit edges are warm gold-brown, never green-tinted; every edge is crisp against the green with a thin dark ink outline.

Lighting is low and warm, falling from above and slightly in front on the right, so the top crust and its front lip glow warm bronze and the underside sinks into deep umber shadow. Colours are given only as guidance; never print them.

Style (required): dark, muted ink on aged paper, like an etched storybook engraving. Etched ink linework with near-black ink outlines; crosshatch and fine line hatching for every shadow and form; visible aged paper grain and fibre texture under all colour; hand-printed, slightly uneven ink. No flat fills, no vector shapes, no smooth digital gradients, no glossy 3D rendering.
